newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Two European diesel cargoes fixed to Asia-traders.
newsitem.headline: Two European diesel cargoes fixed to Asia-traders.

text.p: A U.S. oil trading company has fixed two long-ranged (LR) tankers of gas oil from Europe which might head to Asia, trading sources said on Thursday.
One of the cargoes has been fixed for shipment to India while the destination of the second cargo has yet to be firmed up. "It all depends on the market," one trader said.
In a recent tender, Indian Oil Corp (IOC) awarded one 45,000-tonne cargo to the U.S. trader for delivery in December to the west coast of India.

The two arbitrage cargoes are part of a record 865,100 tonnes of physical gas oil that the U.S. trader is taking delivery upon the expiry of the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) November futures contract on Tuesday.

The Singapore gas oil swaps market had fallen early Wednesday on talk that the two arbitrage cargoes are headed eastwards to $29.60/$29.75 per barrel for December, down 30 cents from Tuesday's levels.
But gas oil swap prices rebounded on Thursday along with the rally on crude futures to trade at $30.30-$30.40.

The physical gas oil market also sustained its strength on Wednesday with a deal done at another five-year record of $30.80 for an early-December lifting cargo, 20 cents over the previous high traded last Friday.

Traders said the arbitrage window is currently satisfactory with gas oil in Asia valued around $14.50 per tonne over levels in Europe. But traders said the east-west spread needs to be around $17-$18 per tonne for the arbitrage to really work.
